gold_target_sql: BEGIN; -- 1) Add a 'status' column to both tables IF it doesn't exist already. -- (PostgreSQL doesn’t have "IF NOT EXISTS" for columns pre-v15, so we do a safe check.) DO $$ BEGIN -- Check if "status" column exists in "curricula". IF NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'curricula' AND column_name = 'status' ) THEN EXECUTE 'ALTER TABLE curricula ADD COLUMN status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''installed'''; END IF; -- Check if "status" column exists in "educational_resources". IF NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'educational_resources' AND column_name = 'status' ) THEN EXECUTE 'ALTER TABLE educational_resources ADD COLUMN status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''installed'''; END IF; END$$; -- 2) Recursively gather all curricula connected to your target (e.g. curriculum_id=1) -- via shared resources, then update them in one pass. Then also update resources. WITH RECURSIVE connected_curricula AS ( -- Base case: pick the single curriculum you want to upgrade SELECT c.curriculum_id FROM curricula c WHERE c.curriculum_id = 1 -- set as needed AND c.status = 'installed' -- only if you want to filter by 'installed' UNION -- (not UNION ALL) to avoid duplicates and infinite loops -- Recursive step: find other curricula that share any resource SELECT cr2.curriculum_id FROM connected_curricula cte JOIN curriculum_resources cr1 ON cr1.curriculum_id = cte.curriculum_id JOIN curriculum_resources cr2 ON cr2.resource_key = cr1.resource_key WHERE cr2.curriculum_id <> cte.curriculum_id ), updated_curricula AS ( UPDATE curricula SET status = 'to upgrade' WHERE curriculum_id IN (SELECT curriculum_id FROM connected_curricula) RETURNING curriculum_id ), updated_resources AS ( UPDATE educational_resources er SET status = 'to upgrade' WHERE er.resource_key IN ( SELECT cr.resource_key FROM curriculum_resources cr JOIN connected_curricula cc ON cr.curriculum_id = cc.curriculum_id ) RETURNING resource_key ) -- 3) Provide a final SELECT of counts, so psycopg2 has results to fetch SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM updated_curricula) AS curricula_updated, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM updated_resources) AS resources_updated; COMMIT
